error_modes.label: TWO-WAY CONTACT AND FREQUENCY MANAGEMENT WITHIN THE FORMATION

texts.0: SP, due to an unrehearsed frequency plan for the departure and area phases, did not maintain R/T contact with the ground station and with the other formation member, with the result that the aircraft stayed on the previous frequency for more than one minute after the briefed change and missed two directive calls from the formation. The IP selected the correct frequency and re-established two-way contact for the SP. Contact with the ground station was regained only after the controller called the formation three times.
texts.1: SP, due to an unrehearsed frequency plan for the departure phase, did not establish two-way contact on the new frequency at the briefed point, with the result that the check-in was transmitted about 20 seconds late and only after the IP pointed out that the formation had already changed frequency. SP then checked in with the correct call and no further prompting was needed. Frequency management stayed at the limit of the acceptable standard for the remainder of the sortie.
texts.2: SP, due to a delayed selection of the preset for the area frequency, did not check in with the formation on the first call, with the result that the check-in was made about 5 seconds after the lead and was corrected on SP's own initiative. SP identified the wrong preset without prompting and re-established contact with both the ground station and the formation before the area entry. No IP intervention was required.
texts.3: SP maintained two-way R/T contact with the ground stations, with the other aircraft concerned and with the other formation member throughout the sortie. Every briefed frequency change was made at the correct point and the check-in followed immediately and in the correct order. No call from the formation or from the ground station went unanswered.
texts.4: SP managed the complete radio plan of the formation sortie without a single late or missed frequency change, including the unbriefed change issued in the recovery phase. Check-ins were transmitted in the correct order and with the correct content on the first attempt in every phase. SP kept simultaneous awareness of the ground station and the intra-formation frequency for the whole mission.
texts.marginal: SP maintained two-way contact within standards, but each frequency change required a visible pause before the check-in and the intra-formation frequency was selected last on every occasion. The trend is toward handling the radios sequentially rather than as a planned set of actions. SP is expected to rehearse the frequency plan during mission preparation so that the changes and check-ins are made without hesitation.

texts_at.1: SP checked in on the new frequency, though the check-in was transmitted about 20 seconds late and only once IP pointed out that the formation had already changed frequency, with the correct call made unaided after that. Performance remained inside the standard required for this stage of training. SP is expected to check in at the briefed point before the verbal prompt on the next sortie.
texts_at.2: SP did not check in with the formation on the first call after a delayed selection of the preset for the area frequency, with the check-in made about 5 seconds after the lead and corrected on the own initiative, identifying the wrong preset without prompting and re-establishing contact with both the ground station and the formation before the area entry, with no IP intervention required. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to select the correct preset before the briefed change so the check-in is not delayed.
texts_at.3: SP maintained two-way contact within standards, though each frequency change required a visible pause before the check-in and the intra-formation frequency was selected last on every occasion, handling the radios sequentially rather than as a planned set of actions. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to rehearse the frequency plan during mission preparation so the changes and check-ins are made without hesitation.

texts_above.2: SP checked in with the formation about 5 seconds after the lead, after a delayed selection of the preset for the area frequency had left the first call missed, identifying the wrong preset without prompting and re-establishing contact with both the ground station and the formation before the area entry, with no prompting from the IP. Selecting the correct preset before the briefed change would remove the delayed check-in entirely. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to good recovery of the area check-in after a preset error.
texts_above.3: SP maintained two-way R/T contact with the ground stations, with the other aircraft concerned and with the other formation member throughout the sortie, with every briefed frequency change made at the correct point and the check-in following immediately and in the correct order, and no call from the formation or from the ground station going unanswered. The only refinement left is to hold the same order into an unbriefed frequency change. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to very good frequency management through the sortie.
texts_above.4: SP managed the complete radio plan of the formation sortie without a single late or missed frequency change, including the unbriefed change issued in the recovery phase, with check-ins transmitted in the correct order and with the correct content on the first attempt in every phase and simultaneous awareness of the ground station and the intra-formation frequency kept for the whole mission. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to excellent management of the complete radio plan.

error_modes.label: FORMAL POSITION REPORTS TO GROUND STATIONS

texts.0: SP, due to an unlearned format for the formation position report, did not give the formal position reports to the ground station, with the result that two reports required at published points were omitted and a third was transmitted with the wrong number of aircraft and the wrong level. The IP dictated the content of the report and finally transmitted it from the rear cockpit. The controller had to request the formation position twice before an accurate report was received.
texts.1: SP, due to an unlearned format for the formation position report, did not transmit the report in the required form at the reporting point, with the result that the call was made about 30 seconds past the point and was completed only after the IP prompted for the missing elements. SP corrected the content after the prompt and the following report was made correctly. Report accuracy remained at the limit of the acceptable standard.
texts.2: SP, due to an incomplete recall of the report elements for the area entry, did not include the formation composition in the first transmission, with the result that the report was incomplete for about 5 seconds until SP amended it unaided. SP identified the omission before the controller asked for it and passed the complete report at the correct point. No prompting from the IP was required.
texts.3: SP contacted the ground stations at every required point and gave the formal position reports in the prescribed form. Position, level, formation composition and intentions were correct and complete in each report. All reports were transmitted at the published points without delay.
texts.4: SP gave every formal position report at the correct point with complete and accurate content on the first transmission, including the report requested off-schedule by the controller. The wording followed the standard format exactly in each case and required no amendment or repetition. SP kept the reported position consistent with the actual position of the formation throughout the sortie.
texts.marginal: SP gave the formal position reports within standards, but the composition and intentions elements were assembled slowly and the reports were transmitted close to the reporting points rather than at them. The trend is toward building the report only when the point is reached. SP is expected to prepare the content of each report in advance so that the transmission is made at the point and without delay.

texts_at.1: SP completed the position report after the missing elements were prompted, though the call was made about 30 seconds past the reporting point and completed only once IP prompted for the missing elements, with the content corrected after the prompt and the following report made correctly. Performance remained inside the standard required for this stage of training. SP is expected to transmit the report in the required form at the reporting point, before the verbal prompt on the next sortie.
texts_at.2: SP left the formation composition out of the first transmission for the area entry after incomplete recall of the report elements, with the report incomplete for about 5 seconds until SP amended it unaided, identifying the omission before the controller asked for it and passing the complete report at the correct point, with no prompting from the IP required. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to recall the complete set of report elements before the reporting point so the amendment is not needed.
texts_at.3: SP gave the formal position reports within standards, though the composition and intentions elements were assembled slowly and the reports were transmitted close to the reporting points rather than at them, building the report only when the point was reached. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to prepare the content of each report in advance so the transmission is made at the point and without delay.

texts_above.2: SP left the formation composition out of the first transmission for the area entry after incomplete recall of the report elements, with the report incomplete for about 5 seconds until SP amended it unaided, identifying the omission before the controller asked for it and passing the complete report at the correct point, with no prompting from the IP. Recalling the complete set of report elements before the reporting point would remove the amendment entirely. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to sound recovery of a report element omitted at the area entry.
texts_above.3: SP contacted the ground stations at every required point and gave the formal position reports in the prescribed form, with position, level, formation composition and intentions correct and complete in each report and all reports transmitted at the published points without delay. The only refinement left is to prepare the same content ahead of a report requested off-schedule. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to sure-handed preparation of every position report.
texts_above.4: SP gave every formal position report at the correct point with complete and accurate content on the first transmission, including the report requested off-schedule by the controller, with the wording following the standard format exactly in each case and requiring no amendment or repetition, and the reported position kept consistent with the actual position of the formation throughout the sortie. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to exceptional accuracy sustained across every position report of the sortie.

error_modes.label: ACCURACY OF THE INFORMATION PASSED TO THE WINGMAN AS LEADER

texts.0: SP, as formation Leader and due to a plan that was not updated after the change of the area allocation, did not provide accurate information to the Wingman, with the result that the direction passed for the area entry contained an incorrect heading and level and was not corrected before the Wingman had followed it. Two further directive calls conflicted with what had been briefed. The IP took the radios and passed the correct information to the Wingman.
texts.1: SP, as formation Leader and due to a plan that was not updated after the change of the area allocation, did not pass accurate information to the Wingman on the first call, with the result that the level given was wrong by 1000 feet and was corrected about 15 seconds later only after the IP pointed out the error. The subsequent directive calls were correct. Accuracy of the information passed to the Wingman remained at the limit of the acceptable standard.
texts.2: SP, as formation Leader and due to reading the sortie card while manoeuvring, did not state the correct turning point in the first directive call, with the result that the information was inaccurate for about 5 seconds before SP amended it unaided. SP corrected the call before the Wingman acted on it and passed all following information accurately. No intervention by the IP was required.
texts.3: SP, as formation Leader, provided the Wingman with accurate information for every phase of the sortie. Headings, levels, speeds and manoeuvre intentions passed by R/T matched the actual plan and the briefed profile. Each directive call was made early enough for the Wingman to act on it.
texts.4: SP, as formation Leader, passed accurate and complete information to the Wingman on the first transmission in every phase, including the two changes issued by the ground station in flight. Every directive call was timed so that the Wingman could comply without any additional manoeuvre. No information passed by SP had to be amended or repeated at any point in the sortie.
texts.marginal: SP passed accurate information to the Wingman within standards, but the directive calls were made late in each case and left the Wingman little time to prepare for the manoeuvre. The trend is toward transmitting the intention at the moment of execution rather than ahead of it. SP is expected to pass the information early enough for the Wingman to comply without a rushed correction.

texts_at.1: SP, as formation Leader, corrected the level given to the Wingman, though the level was wrong by 1000 feet and the correction followed only once IP pointed out the error about 15 seconds later, with the subsequent directive calls correct. Performance remained inside the standard required for this stage of training. SP is expected to pass the correct level on the first call before the verbal prompt on the next sortie.
texts_at.2: SP, as formation Leader, stated the wrong turning point in the first directive call while reading the sortie card during manoeuvring, with the information inaccurate for about 5 seconds before SP amended it unaided, correcting the call before the Wingman acted on it and passing all following information accurately, with no intervention by the IP required. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to update the sortie card before manoeuvring so the turning point is correct on the first call.
texts_at.3: SP, as formation Leader, passed accurate information to the Wingman within standards, though the directive calls were made late in each case and left the Wingman little time to prepare for the maneuver, transmitting the intention at the moment of execution rather than ahead of it. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to pass the information early enough for the Wingman to comply without a rushed correction.

texts_above.2: SP, as formation Leader, stated the wrong turning point in the first directive call while reading the sortie card during manoeuvring, with the information inaccurate for about 5 seconds before SP amended it unaided, correcting the call before the Wingman acted on it and passing all following information accurately, with no prompting from the IP. Updating the sortie card before manoeuvring would remove the inaccurate call entirely. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to solid recovery of a directive call before the Wingman acted on it.
texts_above.3: SP, as formation Leader, provided the Wingman with accurate information for every phase of the sortie, with headings, levels, speeds and maneuver intentions passed by R/T matching the actual plan and the briefed profile, and each directive call made early enough for the Wingman to act on it. The only refinement left is to hold the same accuracy through an unbriefed change of plan. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to well-developed accuracy in every directive call to the Wingman.
texts_above.4: SP, as formation Leader, passed accurate and complete information to the Wingman on the first transmission in every phase, including the two changes issued by the ground station in flight, with every directive call timed so the Wingman could comply without any additional maneuver and no information needing amendment or repetition at any point in the sortie. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to outstanding accuracy sustained across every directive call of the sortie.

error_modes.label: LEADER REMINDERS FOR FUNCTIONAL AIRCRAFT CHECKS AND FUEL CHECK

texts.0: SP, as formation Leader and due to inadequate workload management during the approach phase, did not remind the Wingman of the functional aircraft checks and of the fuel check, with the result that no fuel check was called at any point of the sortie and the formation fuel state was established only when the IP directed the call. The functional checks before the working phase were also omitted. The IP had to run both checks by R/T on SP's behalf.
texts.1: SP, as formation Leader and due to task sequencing that concentrated all cockpit workload inside the turn, did not call the fuel check at the briefed point, with the result that the check was transmitted more than two minutes late and only after the IP prompted for it. SP then obtained the Wingman's fuel state correctly and called the functional checks. Prompting of the formation checks remained at the limit of the acceptable standard.
texts.2: SP, as formation Leader and due to workload concentrated on rejoining the formation, did not call the functional aircraft checks at the planned point, with the result that the call was made about 30 seconds late on SP's own initiative. SP recognised the omission unaided and completed both the functional checks and the fuel check before the working phase. No IP prompting was required.
texts.3: SP, as formation Leader, reminded the Wingman of the functional aircraft checks and of the fuel check at every planned point of the sortie. Each check was called clearly, and SP obtained and acknowledged the Wingman's reply before continuing. The fuel state of the formation was known and current in every phase.
texts.4: SP, as formation Leader, called the functional aircraft checks and the fuel checks at every planned point and additionally before the unbriefed profile change, without any prompting. The replies of the Wingman were obtained, compared with SP's own state and used in the decision on the remaining profile. The formation fuel picture was accurate and shared at all times.
texts.marginal: SP called the functional aircraft and fuel checks within standards, but each call came at the end of a manoeuvre rather than at the planned point of the profile. The trend is toward postponing the formation checks whenever the cockpit workload rises. SP is expected to protect the check calls as fixed points of the profile and to make them regardless of the workload at the time.

texts_at.1: SP, as formation Leader, obtained the Wingman's fuel state and called the functional checks, though the fuel check was transmitted more than two minutes late and only once IP prompted for it, with the subsequent checks completed correctly. Performance remained inside the standard required for this stage of training. SP is expected to call the fuel check at the briefed point before the verbal prompt on the next sortie.
texts_at.2: SP, as formation Leader, called the functional aircraft checks about 30 seconds late on the own initiative after workload concentrated on rejoining the formation delayed the planned call, recognizing the omission unaided and completing both the functional checks and the fuel check before the working phase, with no IP prompting required. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to call the functional checks at the planned point even while rejoining the formation.
texts_at.3: SP, as formation Leader, called the functional aircraft and fuel checks within standards, though each call came at the end of a maneuver rather than at the planned point of the profile, postponing the formation checks whenever the cockpit workload rose. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to protect the check calls as fixed points of the profile and to make them regardless of the workload at the time.

texts_above.2: SP, as formation Leader, called the functional aircraft checks about 30 seconds late on the own initiative after workload concentrated on rejoining the formation delayed the planned call, recognizing the omission unaided and completing both the functional checks and the fuel check before the working phase, with no prompting from the IP. Protecting the check as a fixed point of the profile would remove the delay entirely. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to steady recovery of the formation checks despite the rejoin workload.
texts_above.3: SP, as formation Leader, reminded the Wingman of the functional aircraft checks and of the fuel check at every planned point of the sortie, with each check called clearly and the Wingman's reply obtained and acknowledged before continuing, and the fuel state of the formation known and current in every phase. The only refinement left is to hold the same timing into an unbriefed profile change. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to consistently accurate timing of the functional and fuel checks.
texts_above.4: SP, as formation Leader, called the functional aircraft checks and the fuel checks at every planned point and additionally before the unbriefed profile change, without any prompting, with the replies of the Wingman obtained, compared with the own state and used in the decision on the remaining profile, and the formation fuel picture accurate and shared at all times. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to exemplary integration of the fuel picture into the profile decisions.

error_modes.label: WINGMAN CONFIRMATION OF LEADER INFORMATION AND DIRECTIONS

texts.0: SP, as Wingman and due to non-standard phraseology that left the intention ambiguous, did not confirm the information and directions given by the formation Leader, with the result that three directive calls, including one change of level, received no acknowledgement and the Leader had to repeat each of them. One acknowledgement given did not match the direction actually issued. The IP transmitted the confirmations for the SP.
texts.1: SP, as Wingman and due to an unstandard read-back that did not confirm the actual clearance, did not confirm the Leader's direction in the required form, with the result that the acknowledgement was transmitted about 15 seconds after the call and only after the IP pointed out that a reply was owed. SP then read back the direction correctly and the Leader continued the profile. Confirmation of the Leader's calls remained at the limit of the acceptable standard.
texts.2: SP, as Wingman and due to an abbreviated acknowledgement that omitted the new level, did not confirm the full content of the Leader's direction on the first reply, with the result that the read-back was incomplete for about 5 seconds until SP amended it unaided. SP restated the direction in the correct form before complying with it. No prompting or intervention by the IP was required.
texts.3: SP, as Wingman, confirmed every piece of information and every direction given by the formation Leader. Each acknowledgement was transmitted immediately, in standard phraseology, and reproduced the content of the Leader's call exactly. No direction had to be repeated by the Leader at any point.
texts.4: SP, as Wingman, acknowledged every call from the formation Leader on the first transmission, with a read-back that reproduced the content exactly and identified the aircraft correctly. The confirmations were transmitted without interrupting the Leader's exchanges with the ground station. The Leader never had to repeat or clarify a direction throughout the sortie.
texts.marginal: SP confirmed the Leader's information and directions within standards, but the acknowledgements were reduced to the call sign alone whenever the intra-formation traffic increased. The trend is toward abbreviating the read-back to the point where the received content cannot be verified. SP is expected to keep the confirmation complete and in standard phraseology regardless of the R/T traffic at the time.

texts_at.1: SP, as Wingman, read back the direction correctly, though the read-back followed only once IP pointed out that a reply was owed, about 15 seconds after the call, with the Leader continuing the profile once the correct read-back was given. Performance remained inside the standard required for this stage of training. SP is expected to confirm the Leader's direction in the required form without the verbal prompt on the next sortie.
texts_at.2: SP, as Wingman, omitted the new level from the first reply after an abbreviated acknowledgement, with the read-back incomplete for about 5 seconds until SP amended it unaided, restating the direction in the correct form before complying with it, with no prompting or intervention by the IP required. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to include every element of the direction in the first read-back so the amendment is not needed.
texts_at.3: SP, as Wingman, confirmed the Leader's information and directions within standards, though the acknowledgements were reduced to the call sign alone whenever the intra-formation traffic increased, abbreviating the read-back to the point where the received content cannot be verified. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to keep the confirmation complete and in standard phraseology regardless of the R/T traffic at the time.

texts_above.2: SP, as Wingman, omitted the new level from the first reply after an abbreviated acknowledgement, with the read-back incomplete for about 5 seconds until SP amended it unaided, restating the direction in the correct form before complying with it, with no prompting from the IP. Including every element in the first read-back would remove the amendment entirely. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to dependable recovery of a read-back that first omitted the new level.
texts_above.3: SP, as Wingman, confirmed every piece of information and every direction given by the formation Leader, with each acknowledgement transmitted immediately, in standard phraseology, and reproducing the content of the Leader's call exactly, and no direction having to be repeated by the Leader at any point. The only refinement left is to hold the same completeness under a rising intra-formation traffic load. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to notably good completeness in every read-back given.
texts_above.4: SP, as Wingman, acknowledged every call from the formation Leader on the first transmission, with a read-back that reproduced the content exactly and identified the aircraft correctly, with the confirmations transmitted without interrupting the Leader's exchanges with the ground station, and the Leader never having to repeat or clarify a direction throughout the sortie. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to superior precision in every read-back given to the formation Leader.

error_modes.label: WINGMAN MONITORING OF THE LEADER EXTERNAL COMM AND SAFETY INTERJECTION

texts.0: SP, as Wingman and due to lack of assertiveness in voicing a recognized unsafe condition, did not monitor the Leader's radio communication with the ground station and did not interfere when flight safety demanded it, with the result that an instruction to the formation to descend into conflicting traffic went unchallenged and a traffic advisory addressed to the formation was missed. SP also failed to answer when the ground station called the Wingman directly. The IP made the safety call in place of the SP.
texts.1: SP, as Wingman and due to an unstated request for a repeat of the instruction that was not understood, did not interfere at the point where the Leader had read back a level other than the one issued, with the result that the correction was transmitted about 20 seconds later and only after the IP prompted for it. SP then stated the discrepancy clearly and the formation was re-cleared. Monitoring of the Leader's external communication remained at the limit of the acceptable standard.
texts.2: SP, as Wingman and due to attention held on the formation position during the turn, did not detect the incorrect read-back by the Leader on the first transmission, with the result that the discrepancy stood for about 5 seconds until SP called it unaided. SP stated the correct clearance without prompting and the Leader amended the read-back. No intervention by the IP was required.
texts.3: SP, as Wingman, monitored the Leader's radio communication with the ground stations and with the other aircraft throughout the sortie. SP maintained the clearance picture independently and interfered on R/T only when asked by the Leader or when flight safety required it. Each interjection was correct, brief and made at the right moment.
texts.4: SP, as Wingman, kept an independent and accurate picture of every clearance issued to the formation and identified two discrepancies in the Leader's read-back before the ground station did. Each interjection was made in standard phraseology, at the first opportunity and without blocking any other transmission. SP interfered only where flight safety or the Leader's request justified it, and stayed silent on the frequency otherwise.
texts.marginal: SP monitored the Leader's external communication within standards, but the independent clearance picture was maintained only while the formation was in level flight. The trend is toward dropping the listening watch on the ground station frequency whenever the formation manoeuvres. SP is expected to keep monitoring the Leader's exchanges continuously so that a safety-related discrepancy is detected in any phase of the sortie.

texts_at.1: SP, as Wingman, stated the discrepancy and the formation was re-cleared, though the correction was transmitted about 20 seconds later and only once IP prompted for it. Performance remained inside the standard required for this stage of training. SP is expected to interject on a misread level without the verbal prompt on the next sortie.
texts_at.2: SP, as Wingman, did not detect the Leader's incorrect read-back on the first transmission after attention was held on the formation position during the turn, with the discrepancy standing for about 5 seconds until SP called it unaided, stating the correct clearance without prompting so the Leader amended the read-back, with no intervention by the IP required. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to divide attention between position keeping and the Leader's read-back so the discrepancy is caught on the first transmission.
texts_at.3: SP, as Wingman, monitored the Leader's external communication within standards, though the independent clearance picture was maintained only while the formation was in level flight, dropping the listening watch on the ground station frequency whenever the formation manoeuvred. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to keep monitoring the Leader's exchanges continuously so a safety-related discrepancy is detected in any phase of the sortie.

texts_above.2: SP, as Wingman, did not detect the Leader's incorrect read-back on the first transmission after attention was held on the formation position during the turn, with the discrepancy standing for about 5 seconds until SP called it unaided, stating the correct clearance without prompting so the Leader amended the read-back, with no prompting from the IP. Dividing attention between position keeping and the read-back would remove the missed first transmission entirely. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to assured recovery of a discrepancy in the Leader's read-back.
texts_above.3: SP, as Wingman, monitored the Leader's radio communication with the ground stations and with the other aircraft throughout the sortie, maintaining the clearance picture independently and interfering on R/T only when asked by the Leader or when flight safety required it, with each interjection correct, brief and made at the right moment. The only refinement left is to hold the same independent picture through a manoeuvring phase. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to precise maintenance of the independent clearance picture.
texts_above.4: SP, as Wingman, kept an independent and accurate picture of every clearance issued to the formation and identified two discrepancies in the Leader's read-back before the ground station did, with each interjection made in standard phraseology, at the first opportunity and without blocking any other transmission, interfering only where flight safety or the Leader's request justified it and staying silent on the frequency otherwise. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to first-rate independent monitoring that caught two discrepancies ahead of the ground station.

error_modes.label: STANDARD PHRASEOLOGY AND BREVITY OF THE TRANSMISSIONS

texts.0: SP, due to improvised phrasing used in place of standard phraseology, did not transmit in the format expected and added verbiage that is not required, with the result that four calls carried filler such as 'with you' and 'be advised' while the location and the level were omitted, and the controller queried the formation twice for the missing elements. The IP took the radio and re-transmitted the request in standard form. The frequency was occupied by the repeated exchanges for about 30 seconds.
texts.1: SP, due to improvised phrasing used in place of standard phraseology, did not keep the transmission to the information needed in the format expected, with the result that two calls contained non-standard wording and one omitted the location, and the IP prompted for the standard form before the next transmission. SP repeated the call correctly after the prompt and the remaining calls were acceptable. Phraseology stayed at the limit of the acceptable standard for the rest of the sortie.
texts.2: SP, due to a slip into conversational wording on a congested frequency, did not open the call with the agency and the call sign in the prescribed order, with the result that the transmission was non-standard for about 5 seconds until SP restated it unaided. SP recognised the added verbiage without prompting and passed the request in standard phraseology at the second attempt. No IP intervention was required.
texts.3: SP used standard phraseology on every transmission and gave the controller the information needed, nothing more and nothing less. Calls were built as agency calling, call sign, location and request, and no filler wording was added. No transmission had to be repeated or amended for clarity.
texts.4: SP transmitted in standard phraseology throughout the sortie, including the two unbriefed requests made in the area, and every call carried the required elements in the correct order at the first attempt. No non-required verbiage entered any transmission even on the congested recovery frequency. Where a controller phrase was not understood, SP clarified it in plain language without cluttering the frequency.
texts.marginal: SP kept phraseology within standards, but the wording was assembled on the frequency and short filler phrases appeared whenever the request was longer than one line. The trend is toward composing the call while transmitting rather than before keying the microphone. SP is expected to build the content of each call before transmission so that brevity and standard format are kept under congestion.

texts_at.1: SP repeated the call correctly after the prompt for standard form, though two calls initially carried non-standard wording and one omitted the location, with the correction following only once IP prompted for the standard form before the next transmission. Performance remained inside the standard required for this stage of training. SP is expected to open with the agency and call sign in the prescribed order before the verbal prompt on the next sortie.
texts_at.2: SP did not open the call with the agency and the call sign in the prescribed order after a slip into conversational wording on a congested frequency, with the transmission non-standard for about 5 seconds until SP restated it unaided, recognizing the added verbiage without prompting and passing the request in standard phraseology at the second attempt, with no IP intervention required. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to open with the agency and the call sign on the first attempt so the restatement is not needed.
texts_at.3: SP kept phraseology within standards, though the wording was assembled on the frequency and short filler phrases appeared whenever the request was longer than one line, composing the call while transmitting rather than before keying the microphone. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to build the content of each call before transmission so brevity and standard format are kept under congestion.

texts_above.2: SP restated the call in the prescribed order after a slip into conversational wording on a congested frequency had left the opening non-standard for about 5 seconds, recognizing the added verbiage without prompting and passing the request in standard phraseology at the second attempt, with no prompting from the IP. Building the call before keying the microphone would remove the restatement entirely. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to competent recovery of a non-standard opening under a congested frequency.

texts.2: SP, due to hesitation over the correct signal for the failure, did not pass it on the first attempt after moving to route, with the result that the exchange took about 5 seconds longer than required before SP selected and gave the correct signal unaided. texts_at.1: SP moved to route, rocked the wings and passed the signal, which was acknowledged, though the correct sequence followed only once IP prompted for it about twenty seconds after the failure had been identified. Performance remained inside the standard required for this stage of training. SP is expected to attract attention before giving the visual signal, before the verbal prompt on the next sortie.
texts_at.2: SP was hesitant over the correct signal for the failure and did not pass it on the first attempt after moving to route, with the exchange taking about 5 seconds longer than required before SP selected and gave the correct signal unaided, holding route position and moving no closer until directed, with no IP intervention required. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to select the correct signal before the first attempt so the extra seconds are not needed.
texts_at.3: SP handled the no radio case within standards, though the failure was confirmed only after several further attempts to transmit, and the visual signal was given before the attention of the other aircraft had clearly been obtained, persisting with a failed radio instead of moving to the visual signal procedure. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to recognize the total failure early, move to route and attract attention before signalling.

texts_above.2: SP was hesitant over the correct signal for the failure and did not pass it on the first attempt after moving to route, with the exchange taking about 5 seconds longer than required before SP selected and gave the correct signal unaided, holding route position and moving no closer until directed, with no prompting from the IP. Selecting the correct signal before the first attempt would remove the extra seconds entirely. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to competent recovery of the correct signal for the failure.
texts_above.3: SP recognized the total radio failure, manoeuvred from close formation to route, attracted the attention of the other aircraft and showed the appropriate visual signal, retaining the Number 2 position and rejoining no closer than route until directed, with the pattern and the landing flown on the visual signals passed by the other aircraft. The only refinement left is to hold the same recognition on a failure that develops more gradually. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to disciplined execution of the no radio sequence from recognition to landing.
texts_above.4: SP identified the radio failure at once, took up the Number 2 position and passed the appropriate visual signal after attracting the attention of the other aircraft at the first attempt, acknowledging every subsequent signal with a head nod, holding route position until directed closer and assuming landing clearance only on the signal from the other aircraft, and where a knock-it-off was required with the radio out, signalled it with a continuous wing rock. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to faultless execution of the complete no radio sequence from failure to landing clearance.
